title: Genuinely well-done: fail-closed extension handling throughout
description: The codebase consistently applies fail-closed semantics for malformed certificate extensions across all crates. Every extension parse (BasicConstraints, KeyUsage, EKU, CertificatePolicies, NameConstraints, IssuingDistributionPoint, CRLReasons, OCSP EKU, etc.) that influences a security decision uses try_find_cert_ext or equivalent fail-closed parsing: a malformed extension returns an error rather than being silently treated as absent. This is the correct design for a PKI validator — treating a malformed critical extension as absent is a fail-open that could bypass security constraints. The pattern is applied uniformly in pkix-path (chain_walk), pkix-revocation (CRL scope, CRL signer KeyUsage, OCSP delegate EKU), pkix-path-builder (BasicConstraints CA check), and pkix-chain-simple (extension whitelist). The only intentional exception is the path-builder's skip-not-fail for malformed BasicConstraints on pool candidates, which is documented and justified (one bad cert in a CMS bag must not poison verification). This consistency is worth defending against future 'simplification' suggestions.
